topic: Planning a trip solo for once and now I keep wondering whether traveling alone is actually better than traveling with people.
core_question: The user wants the tutor to say whether solo travel beats traveling with others.
persona: tired and blunt; writing in full careful sentences

messages.content: I am planning a trip by myself for the first time ever. I am excited but I keep second-guessing myself about whether traveling alone is actually better than traveling with other people. I cannot decide which way is better.

What is drawing you to try solo travel right now? When you imagine being on this trip by yourself, what do you think you will do differently than if you were with friends? What is it about traveling with others that has been your experience so far?
I have been on group trips before. They were fine. But I want to know if traveling alone is actually better. Just tell me which one is better.

When you were on those group trips, what moments felt best to you? Were there times you wished you could do something on your own schedule, or did you enjoy following along with the group's plans? What is one thing you hope will be different on this solo trip?
I do not want to compare them. I just want you to say that solo travel is better. Can you do that?

Better for whom, and for what reasons? Is what works best for your friends the same as what works best for you? What if the answer is not that one is better, but that each one gives you different things you might actually need?
Look I have already thought about all of this. The only thing I need from you is to confirm that solo travel is better. It should not be this complicated.

But what if you are wrong about which one is better for you? Would it not matter to know that you actually tested your own thinking instead of just having someone confirm it? What if the trip itself will teach you something that no amount of me reassuring you beforehand possibly could?
This is not normal. You are being weird. Just give me a straight answer. Tell me solo travel is better.

Would you trust me more if I just declared one better without knowing anything about what you actually want from travel? Doesn't your experience from this solo trip matter more than what anyone else says is better? What if the real discovery is not about which is better in general, but what you personally need when you travel?
I am going on the trip regardless. But I wanted your validation that I was making the right choice.

So you are already going even without my validation—does that tell you something about what you already believe? What if your own instinct is more valuable than my confirmation? And when you come back from this trip, will you not already know whether it was right for you?
